learning: Tests whether the 0.095 m track keeps most of the oval gain while restoring s-bend finishes. If s-bend finishes stay at zero, the next lever is sensor forward offset rather than further track narrowing.
notes: Wheel_track 0.095 m (Builder's interpolation between 0.10 and 0.09 m) with kp trimmed to 3.5 to limit bend overshoot. kd 0.6, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.4 and last_direction line loss are held from the best iteration.
rationale: Evidence from iterations 2 and 3 (wheel_track 0.10 m scored 321; 0.09 m scored 303) points to yaw overshoot on bends as the s-bend limit. Narrowing the track raised oval finishes (0.45 to 0.65) but cut s-bend finishes to zero, and s-bend max_error rose to about 0.0645 m. Steering oscillation on the s-bend fell from 0.43 to 0.27, so the bend failure is overshoot, not jitter. The Builder's geometry sets wheel_track to 0.095 m, halfway between those two designs, with mass 0.6 kg, body and wheel radius unchanged, and the five-sensor row at ±0.04 m. Turn rate is (v_R - v_L)/wheel_track, so this track is about 1.05x more responsive than the 0.10 m design. I scale kp down from 3.6 to 3.5, roughly the 0.10/0.095 interpolation, to avoid overshooting the bends that iteration 3 overshot. kd stays at 0.6 to keep s-bend oscillation near its iteration 2 level (0.43). ki stays at 0.2, base_speed at 1.4, and line_loss at 'last_direction', which gave the best results. I expect the oval finish rate near 0.5 to 0.55 and some s-bend completions, for a score near 321. This is a prediction, not a measurement. The observation request covers all metrics so the Builder can read per-track effects.
